messages.author: 4e69b94a09c8cf3b
messages.subject: Re: Stacked graph
parts:
Should you be turning freq into a fraction of the whole? The percent
formatter expects a fraction it can multiply by 100. Not sure why your
legend is not showing up. Get rid of the reference to the data frame in
the geom_bar aesthetic.

x$frequey = x$freq/sum(x$freq)

ggplot(x, aes(x = variable,fill=factor(value))) +
geom_bar(aes(weight=frequey))+
coord_flip() +
scale_fill_manual(value = rev(brewer.pal(7, "Greens"))) +
scale_y_continuous("percent",format="percent")

parts: Hi:

On Sat, Sep 25, 2010 at 5:51 PM, Felipe <felipel...@gmail.com> wrote:
scale_fill_discrete("Label") worked well


More one question

sumpacg <- ggplot(sum, aes(factor(sumpacnormalizada)))
sumpacg + geom_histogram()  + scale_y_continuous("Number of subjects")
+ scale_x_discrete("Global Scale")
In a histogram, the x variable is continuous. You have set it to be a factor, so you should be using a bar chart instead.

here and in other histogram, the breaks in x discrete only works for
values that i have in the vector, i mean
only values that sumpacnormalizada has it shows, any other...

by the way, it should be a continuous scale this vector, why it only
accepts discrete in x? And how can i put in intervals the break? Like
30-40-50-60-70
i found a break by quartile, it should have one by intervals of 5 or
10 or something, and not onyl values the vector assumes..
any other person had this problem before?

If x is continuous and you're using geom_histogram(), set the option binwidth manually. See the on-line help of geom_histogram() for examples:

http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/geom_histogram.html


HTH,
Dennis

Tks
